feedback: Approved for racing. The candidate is the iteration-5 best design (score 160.17) with one controller change: ki 0.2 to 0.3. Geometry (y=0.07 sensors, x values, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], sensor_size 0.012), kp 2.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.0 and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged, so the race isolates the integral effect. The evidence behind it: iteration 5 raised progress on the oval (0.67) and s-bend (0.31) with forward sensors, but slalom progress fell slightly (0.113 vs 0.125 in iteration 4), and mean max_error stayed near 0.06 on every track. That pattern fits a fixed left/right motor mismatch, which the integral term is meant to cancel. Iteration 4 showed that gain changes alone did not move bend progress, so testing ki is the right next lever. This candidate is valid, is a minimal change to the best raced build, and gives telemetry that the next revision can use, so it is approved now. Read the race as follows. If s-bend and slalom progress rise above 0.31 and 0.125 with oval steering_oscillation at or below 0.283, keep ki 0.3 and then test a small base_speed increase (1.0 to 1.1) while watching max_error. If progress falls, or s-bend steering_oscillation rises well above 0.21, the larger integral is adding overshoot: return ki to 0.2 and test kd 0.35 instead. Survival still comes before speed, so do not raise base_speed while any track ends off track early.
requested_changes: After race 6: if s-bend progress exceeds 0.31 and slalom progress exceeds 0.125 with oval steering_oscillation at or below 0.283, keep ki 0.3 and try controller.base_speed 1.1 with kd 0.4 and kp 2.5, since survival is holding.

After race 6: if progress drops on the s-bend or slalom, or s-bend steering_oscillation rises well above 0.21, the extra integral is causing overshoot. Return controller.ki to 0.2 and test controller.kd 0.35 instead, keeping y=0.07.

After race 6: if max_error stays near 0.06 on every track with ki 0.3, the mismatch is not the limit. Keep geometry at y=0.07 and try controller.kp 3.0 with ki 0.3, since iteration 3 showed lower kp did not hurt progress.
